decision_reason: NASA identifies TIE as an open-source 0.4 product and links this exact public repository; the source README says it was deployed as part of NASA GIBS, and the repository carries Apache-2.0. However, GitHub says the repo was archived in 2018 and describes TIE as deprecated. NASA's product page calls the release 0.4 while the last code commits describe 0.5/0.6, and the README offers no install/run guide. Current code-to-product parity, current support, and enough user guidance for a mature reusable archived product are not established; hold rather than infer from the NASA catalog listing.

government_provenance.note: NASA's official Software Catalog identifies TIE 0.4 as software for the NASA Global Imagery Browse Services project and its Download Now link points to this exact repository. The README independently says TIE was deployed as part of NASA GIBS.

public_source.note: The archived but publicly readable repository exposes source, README, and license without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact root LICENSE is the OSI-approved Apache License 2.0. The first functional-source push is dated 2016-03-10; the earlier initial commit added LICENSE, so the Apache grant was present when the executable project files were first publicly pushed.

primary_evidence.note: The catalog identifies TIE 0.4 and links this repository, but the repo is owner-archived and explicitly deprecated. Its last source history refers to TIE 0.6, and there is no current product-specific support/use signal or README-level install/run guidance establishing source parity or a reusable historical release.

decision_reason: NASA Worldview is an independently usable NASA ESDIS application currently deployed at NASA's official Earthdata site. Its public repository is the exact application source; the README describes the operational imagery browser and gives concrete installation, build, run, configuration, and user documentation. The exact NASA-1.3 agreement identifies NASA/GSFC and the original Worldview software designation. The first grant-bearing public-source commit dates to 2014 and modifies functional source along with adding the NASA agreement. All four checks pass; current production use and active source work support Active status.
